To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the impact of pyrethroid insecticides on dung fauna can be minimised by using only the insecticide in the form of a spray; and (ii) the impact can be further minimised by applying the spray to the legs and abdomen of cattle.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the use of pyrethroids as cattle treatments for tse-tse fly control and the impact of such treatments on the fauna of the cattle dung which plays an important role in the soil fertility of African savannahs.
the development of methods of treating cattle for the control of tsetse flies, the vectors of African trypanosomiasis, which have minimal impact on the dung fauna.
the development and implementation of a sustainable and cost-effective approach for the control of tsetse flies in Zimbabwe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
restricted applications of deltamethrine on the legs of cattle can be used to control tsetse without having any adverse impact on dung fauna.

1) the use of pour-on formulations of pyrethroids on the back of cattle is not recommended, 2) the use of a spray formulation of deltamethin applied to the legs and the belly of cattle is recommended for tsetse treatment, 3) the use of deltamethirn spray applied to the legs alone is a cost effective alternative for tsetse treatments.

The restricted application of the spray formulation of deltamethrins to the legs of cattle is the best option for minimising the adverse impact of insecticide on the dung fauna, and hence for promoting dung fauna and improving soil fertility in areas treated for tsetse.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of deltamethrine on the legs and belly of cattle can reduce the impact of pyrethroid use on dung fauna and so on soil fertility.
it is possible to reduce the impact on dung beetles and other dung fauna, and hence improve the soil fertility, by treating cattle with pyrethrins for tsetse flies.
it is possible to reduce the impact on dung beetles by using the pour-on or spray formulation, but that the pour-on is preferable as it is easier to apply.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the impact on dung beetle fauna can be minimised by restricting application of insecticide to the legs and/or belly of the cattle, and using a spray rather than a pour-on formulation.
the use of pour-on formulations should be avoided.
the impact of pyrethroids on dung fauna can be reduced by restricting the use of pyrethroid formulations to those which are applied to the legs and abdomen of cattle.
